clue.text: Tree specially hollowed out happened to hide soldiers

indicators.note: a word hollowed out loses its insides, so only the outer letters of specially remain
one word hiding another holds it within itself

parts.note: happened means came, as in 'it came about'
OR stands for other ranks, i.e. ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A tree, cleverly hollowed, turned out to be concealing troops, like a wooden horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially hollowed out' reads like a description of the tree trunk, but 'hollowed out' keeps just the first and last letters; 'to hide' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a broad-leaved maple species, so it is one example of a tree.

clue.text: Revolutionary at large caught by North American leader

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the whole build is read backwards
being caught by something means being held within it

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US citizen
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A rebel on the run is arrested by a leader from North America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for the fugitive, but it reverses the whole build; 'caught by' makes the North American pair hold 'at large'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is a Muslim sovereign or ruler, so the title fits a leader.

clue.text: Set up company with new number

parts.note: a figure is a number, as in a six-figure sum

explanation.surface: A business is founded with a fresh telephone number.
explanation.definitionFit: To configure a system is to arrange or set it up for use.

clue.text: Wrongly identify false claims ultimately real

indicators.note: false letters are not genuine, so the word claims is rearranged into a new order
ultimately points to the final letter of real

explanation.surface: A paradox: claims that are false turn out in the end to be real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' rearranges CLAIMS into MISCAL; 'ultimately' adds the L that ends real.
explanation.definitionFit: To miscall something is to give it the wrong name, i.e. misname it.

clue.text: A lot of sheep across Spain

indicators.note: the sheep stretch across the country, so its letter sits within them

parts.note: rams are male sheep
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Plenty of sheep are spread across the Spanish countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Reams, originally bundles of paper, informally means a large quantity of anything.

clue.text: Project a very loud voice

parts.note: FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud
air means to voice, as in airing an opinion

explanation.surface: An instruction to project the voice very loudly, as an actor might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' looks like a verb for throwing the voice; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or undertaking, so a project or business in hand.

clue.text: Wild consumer on account of long time on end of blower

parts.note: for means because of, as in 'jailed for theft'
an age is a very long time

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of blower

explanation.surface: Someone eats wildly for ages because of the telephone, British slang 'blower'.
explanation.definitionFit: A forager eats what is gathered from the wild, so it is a consumer of wild food.

clue.text: Is this crossword compiler fit friend?

parts.note: the setter, speaking as I, would phrase this question as 'am I'
a go is a bout or turn, like a fit of something

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether they are healthy enough, addressing a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is this crossword compiler' turns into the setter's own words AM I.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English for a pal.

clue.text: Capturing back upset duchess imprisoned by group

indicators.note: something imprisoned by another is shut up inside it

parts.note: a ring is a group, as in a spy ring

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word on its head, so Kate is read backwards

parts.note: Kate was Duchess of Cambridge before becoming Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A distressed duchess, held by a gang, is being rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: The duchess is Kate, Duchess of Cambridge; 'upset' turns her name over and 'imprisoned by' puts it inside the group.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaking a town means recapturing it, taking it back after losing it.

clue.text: One carrying flyers showing black cosmetic

parts.note: jet is a deep black, from the black gemstone
liner is eye or lip make-up

explanation.surface: A flight attendant shows off her black eyeliner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyers' look like leaflets being carried; they are air passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet airliner carries passengers, so it transports people who fly.

clue.text: Painter left with someone like Houdini, heading off

parts.note: and means with, joining two things

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: Harry Houdini was a famous escape artist

explanation.surface: A painter is left in the company of an escapologist who is departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the first letter E from ESCAPE ARTIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape artist paints scenery, so is one kind of painter.

clue.text: Criticise popular article all about brutish people

indicators.note: all about turns the whole build round so it reads backwards

parts.note: to slam is to criticise harshly
in means popular, as in the in thing
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a popular article about thuggish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all about' reverses SLAM IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling people animals describes them as beasts, coarse and violent.

clue.text: Stage argument backing king demanding toil

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word row is reversed

parts.note: a row is a quarrel
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A theatrical row backs a king who is a hard taskmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Legwork is the laborious routine work behind a project, so drudgery or toil.

clue.text: Lie uncontrollably with blunt report

indicators.note: letters behaving uncontrollably are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lies freely in a bluntly worded report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontrollably' rearranges LIE plus BLUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news statement, a kind of report.

clue.text: Ragged cuddly toy with stuff inside but no head

indicators.note: inside places the stuff within the toy

parts.note: a ted is a teddy bear

indicators.note: no head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: matter is stuff, physical material

explanation.surface: A cuddly toy with its stuffing showing and its head missing is ragged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no head' beheads the stuff, not the toy, and 'inside' places the remainder within the teddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattered clothes are torn and worn to shreds, so ragged.

clue.text: Survey characters protected in our economy

indicators.note: the letters are sheltered inside the clue's run of words our economy

explanation.surface: A survey finds certain people shielded in Britain's economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters protected in' hides the answer in 'ouR ECONomy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Recon is short for reconnaissance, a military survey of territory.

clue.text: Cool cop more casual with us

indicators.note: a casual arrangement is loose and random, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relaxed police officer is friendlier with us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casual' rearranges COP MORE US.
explanation.definitionFit: Composure is calm self-control; to keep your cool is to keep it.

clue.text: Free of charge, second-hand fencing son fixed

parts.note: FOC is the commercial abbreviation for free of charge

indicators.note: fencing means surrounding, as a fence encloses a field

parts.note: second-hand goods are used

explanation.surface: Free second-hand fencing for a son's garden was put up.
explanation.definitionFit: A focussed gaze is fixed, concentrated on one point.

clue.text: Plain old Hitchcock film I go to skip

indicators.note: to skip something is to leave it out

parts.note: Vertigo is a 1958 Alfred Hitchcock thriller

explanation.surface: A plain old Hitchcock film is one I'll miss going to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to skip' removes I and GO from VERTIGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and plainly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: Balcony initially terrified the Queen and family

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of terrified

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
a race is a family line or lineage

explanation.surface: The Queen and her family stand terrified on a palace balcony.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre or stadium the terrace is a raised tier, much like a balcony.

clue.text: Annoying occasion involving order shop oddly overlooked

indicators.note: one word involving another holds it inside

parts.note: time means occasion, as in 'that time'

indicators.note: the odd letters of order shop are passed over, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: An irritating event where a call to order the shop is unaccountably ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly overlooked' drops the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of 'order shop', keeping the even ones; 'involving' puts those inside the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means tedious or irksome, causing annoyance.

clue.text: Learns about ordinary Italian city

indicators.note: about signals moving the letters around into a new order

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: Someone finds out about an ordinary Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges LEARNS into SALERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno is a port city in Campania, southern Italy.

clue.text: Webs appear around empty houses to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means reading upwards, so backwards
around means enclosing the next part

parts.note: to seem is to appear

indicators.note: an empty word has its middle removed, keeping only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Cobwebs show up around abandoned houses in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps just the ends of houses, 'around' wraps appear about them, and 'to the north' reads the result upwards, as fits a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Meshes are net-like structures of interlaced strands, as are webs.

clue.text: Growth of delivery service force

parts.note: UPS is United Parcel Service, a parcel delivery firm
to urge is to force or press

explanation.surface: A courier firm expanding forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: An upsurge is a sudden rise or increase, so growth.

clue.text: Foil is pointed stick for sport

definitions.meaning: one of the three spiked uprights of a cricket wicket

explanation.surface: A fencing foil is a sharp-tipped weapon used in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foil' suggests the fencing sword; it is the verb meaning thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: Stump means to baffle; in cricket the stumps are pointed rods driven into the pitch.

clue.text: Look to leave local area for Italian food

indicators.note: to leave means the letters go out of the word

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Seeking Italian food, go out of the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes LO from local, giving CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A calzone is a folded, stuffed pizza, a dish from Italy.

clue.text: Game played with ball at clubs in Switzerland

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
CH is the vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A ball game played at clubs in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Catch is a simple pastime of throwing a ball back and forth.

clue.text: Kneaded dough — the Quakers just made it

indicators.note: kneading works dough into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Quakers knead dough, and the bakers only just succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kneaded' rearranges DOUGH THE QUAKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeak through is to pass or succeed by the narrowest margin.

clue.text: Party by coastal structure is comparatively stupid

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a pier is a structure jutting out to sea

explanation.surface: A party held on a pier is rather daft.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopey means dim-witted; the comparative form describes someone sillier.

clue.text: They bung openings in the hull beside people in boat

indicators.note: openings are the starting letters of the two words the and hull

parts.note: rowers are people propelling a boat

explanation.surface: People in a boat plug the holes in its hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bung' looks like plugging a hole; it is British slang for throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Bung is informal British for toss, so those who bung things are throwers.
